newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks seen opening flat, hungry for data.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks seen opening flat, hungry for data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were set for a mostly flat opening Thursday, but could move lower at the opening bell if weekly jobless claims came in strong.

"I would suspect a flat opening. If the jobless claims put pressure on bonds, we could open lower, but if no pressure, then at best we're looking for a flat opening," said Peter Cardillo," director of research at Westfalia Investments.
Jobless claims for the week of August 31 are due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists expect them around 335,000, compared with 331,000 last week.
"People will be looking at the weekly jobless claims to give any hint to tomorrow's payroll data," said Cardillo.
August payroll data are due Friday, including the unemployment rate and average hourly earnings, which may provide clues about whether the Fed will raise interest rates.
"Also July housing completions are due (Thursday) and the ECRI report, but the market is really going to be focused on tomorrow's numbers," he said.
July housing completions are due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. The Economic Cycle Research Institute (ECRI) releases a weekly Future Inflation Gauge on Thursdays at 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
"It should basically be in a holding pattern similar to yesterday as we wait around for Friday's job numbers," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
"The price of oil has given up a little ground, so oil stocks might also give back a little," he said.
October Brent crude futures and gas oil futures were trading lower in early London trading.
"Negative preannouncements could also influence the proceedings," Wachtel said. After the market close Wednesday, Kellogg Co, Zilog Inc and InterVoice warned of disappointing third-quarter earnings.
Shares in Mobil Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co and Exxon Corp slipped in London trading.
The benchmark 30-year treasury bond was off 3/32 to yield 7.11 percent.
Japan's Nikkei 225 average closed higher, fueled by a wide range of buying in public funds. In London, the FTSE 100 index was trading near day's peak, up 10.8 to 2,883.5.
The dollar was near the upper end of an intraday range in European trading, near 109 yen and above 1.48 German marks in subdued trading.
Standard & Poor's Futures were off 0.65 to 655.95, indicating a slightly lower opening.

Some short sellers are betting on Cityscape Financial Corp because of its ties to John Peter Galanis, a former tax-shelter promoter, according to the Wall Street Journal's "Heard on the Street" column.

Federal prosecutors have filed charges accusing some brokers of accepting bribes in order to steer their clients into buying the stock of Metal Recovery Technologies Inc, formerly named Malvy Technology, according to the New York Times "Marketplace" column.
